chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sayyari from Abu Suleiman al-Khawwas from al-Fadl ibn Dukayn from Sadir al-Sayrafi who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and upon me was a white sandal. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sadir! What is this sandal? Did you wear it knowingly?' I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you!' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who enters the market intending a white sandal, will not wear it out until he acquires wealth from where he does not expect.' Abu Nu'aym said, 'Sadir informed me that he did not wear out that sandal until he acquired one hundred dinars from where he did not expect.'

key_terms.مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ: from where he does not expect

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of wearing or buying a white sandal according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the specific intention (*niyyah*) behind a mundane purchase to divine providence (*rizq*), illustrating the Shia concept that conscious devotion in daily acts invites unexpected sustenance. The narrative highlights the spiritual significance of intentionality, where the act of seeking a white sandal becomes a vessel for receiving wealth from unforeseen sources, a theme resonant with the promise of 'sufficient provision' in the Quran.
